newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian police let demonstrators pass.
newsitem.headline: Albanian police let demonstrators pass.

text.p: Albanian riot police on Wednesday gave up attempts to disperse a large demonstration in this southern city and let protesters continue their march against the collapse of get-rich-quick pyramid savings funds.
Some of the police appeared to join the crowd, taking off their helmets and handing out cigarettes. "Peace, peace, the police are with us," some of the large crowd chanted.

Earlier police and demonstrators hurled stones at each other after the security forces sought to break up a crowd of around 7,000 which had gathered to demand full refunds following the cave-in of a pyramid scheme popular in the area.
Police fired shots into the air and used dogs and water cannon to move away the crowd, but many demonstrators fought back and eventually broke the 300-strong police cordon.
"We have nowhere to go, there's no police station here, we're tired and hungry," one policeman said. "The people understand."
An earlier attempt to break up the demonstrators also failed and thousands more people joined the crowd during the afternoon, including children and people on crutches.

Wednesday's demonstration was the first large-scale protest in Albania for over a week. Widespread rioting swept the Balkan state last month following the collapse of a number of high-yield investment schemes.
